prs.title: fix: use os.dup to avoid closing real stdin/stdout in stdio_server
prs.author: xlyoung
prs.reason: [llm pick] cluster primary for issue #1933: All four PRs have unknown CI, so the tiebreak is test coverage. #2737 is the only one with 3 files changed, which is the strongest signal that a test was added alongside the fix; the others (1–2 files) likely contain only the fix and possibly a changelog. On technical approach, #2737's use of os.dup() is the correct Unix-level solution: it hands the transport a duplicate file descriptor so that when the transport closes it, the real process stdin/stdout fds are untouched. members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2450: anyio.BrokenResourceError is not caught in stdout_reader, so a race condition — the caller exiting stdio_client while the subprocess is still writing — surfaces as an unhandled exception. clusters.pick_reason: PR #2703 is the only one that fixes both the base class (McpError.__reduce__ reconstructs from self.error) and the subclass (UrlElicitationRequiredError.__reduce__ reconstructs from the message string), using the standard __reduce__ protocol directly on each class. PR #2555 (same base commit f153ea319d as #2478) covers only the subclass, leaving the base class broken; its __reduce__ reconstructs from (self._elicitations, self.message) which preserves the typed elicitations list — a valid approach, but incomplete. PR #2478 (same base as #2555) introduces an external _restore_mcp_error helper rather than placing __reduce__ on the classes themselves, an unusual pattern, and the shown diff does not include a __reduce__ on MCPError itself. #2703 targets the v1.x base (4943114912) so it will need a rebase onto main, but its two-class coverage and clean per-class __reduce__ implementation make it the right shape to adopt.
